Brief Hospital Course:
Mrs. ___ was admitted to ___ on ___ and underwent an 
elective left total shoulder replacement. Pre-operatively, she 
was consented, prepped, and brought to the operating room. 
Intra-operatively, she was closely monitored and remained 
hemodynamically stable. She tolerated the surgical procedure 
well without any difficulty or complication. Full details may be 
found in the patients medical record.  Post-operatively, she was 
transferred to the PACU and floor in stable condition for 
further recovery and nursing care. On the floor, she remained 
hemodynamically stable and her pain was controlled. On POD#2 she 
had a slightly increased temperature, therefore a urine was 
sent, which showed positive leukocytes and 56 WBC's; urine 
culture was negative. She progressed with physical therapy to 
improve her strength and mobility. She continued to make steady 
progress. She was discharged to home with home physical therapy 
in stable condition.

Discharge Instructions:
Keep the dressing clean and dry. Apply a dry sterile dressing as 
needed for drainage or comfort. 

If you experience any shortness of breath, chest pain, increased 
redness, swelling, pain, drainage from incision, temperature 
>101, numbness, tingling, or change in circulation to operative 
extremity, please call your doctor or go to the emergency room 
for evaluation. 

You may not bear weight on your left arm. 

You may resume all of the medications you took prior to your 
hospital admission and take them as prescribed by your doctor. 

Physical Therapy:
Non-weight bearing to left upper extremity.
Left shoulder pendulums.  
Passive ROM left shoulder. 
Active and passive ROM left elbow, wrist, and hand.
Treatments Frequency:
Apply a dry sterile dressing daily.  Keep incision clean and 
dry. 
Your skin staples/sutures may be removed 2 weeks after your 
surgery or at the time of your follow up visit.

Please wear the sling and continue doing left arm pendulums.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Left TSA status post implant.

LEFT SHOULDER, SINGLE AP PORTABLE VIEW.

The patient is status post placement of a left total shoulder prosthesis.  On
this single AP view, the humeral and glenoid components are in overall
anatomic alignment.  Soft tissue swelling, subcutaneous emphysema about the
joint, and skin staples,are seen, all compatible with recent surgery.

Correlation with real-time findings and, when appropriate, conventional
radiographs is recommended for further assessment.
